topic: what happens during coin quality control

sources.title: U.S. Mint Coin Production
supports: Purchased planchets are checked against specifications.
An inspector examines samples after striking for errors.
Some circulating coins failing standards are diverted to a waffler before recycling.
After inspection, circulating coins are counted and weighed.
sources.limits: Applies to the Mint process described, not a universal rule for all producers or products.

sources.title: U.S. Mint Superior Manufacturing Reduces Errors
sources.limits: Historical background; no universal or current metric is quoted.

outline: Inspect coin samples after the press
Separate coin production checks from collector grading
Check accepted coin output after inspection
Understand what coin quality control confirms
